75% Hydration Sourdough Calculator

A 500 g country loaf starts here at 75% hydration, 20% starter, and 2% salt. Change hydration if this feels too wet or too stiff. Wet your hands before you shape, and pull the skin tight so the round holds.

Percentages are of the flour you weigh out, and effective hydration also counts the flour and water inside a starter that is itself 100% hydration.

How to adjust to 73%

Here 73% means the water divided by the flour you weigh. It does not count the flour and water already inside the starter. Keep 500 g flour, 100 g starter, and 10 g salt, and use 365 g water. The dough weighs 975 g. If you type 73 in the hydration field, the effective hydration line above shows about 75.5%. That is normal. The calculator treats the 100 g starter as 100% hydration, so it counts 50 g flour and 50 g water inside the starter. If you want the effective hydration itself to be about 73%, use about 352 g water. Then (352 + 50) / (500 + 50) is 73.1%.

The dough feels a little firmer than at 75%, so it is easier to tighten into a round. In the first 2 hours, give it three stretch-and-folds instead of four. Start checking the bulk around 4 hours at about 24°C (75°F). Dust the bench more lightly when you shape, and still pull the skin taut before the cold rest.
